messages:
Incident Bot: Pager duty alert — SEV2: node-ssd-3 disk pressure. Affected pods: inference-runtime-*, modelcache-*. Triggered at 2025-10-12T02:00:34Z
SRE Jae: got the page, checking cluster metrics and node conditions
Eng Oncall - Mira: I see node-ssd-3 at 98% ephemeral usage, kubelet eviction threshold reached. Several inference-runtime pods got Evicted with ExitCode 137.
SRE Jae: 137 -> OOM? Could be caused by eviction during writeback. Are we seeing CUDA errors in crashed containers?
Eng Oncall - Mira: Logs show runtime crashed with: "CUDA error: out of memory (700)" after model cache restore attempts. Also lots of logwrite errors: "ENOSPC: no space left on device"
Platform Mike: Looks like logs + modelcache shard writes filled /var/lib/kubelet/pods/*/volumes/ephemeral. Some pods haven't rotated logs in last 3 days (huge growth).
SRE Jae: Estimating blast radius — how many customers? per-route metrics show increased 500s for 2 hosted tenants hitting models served from that node.
Customer Success - Lina: I'm pinging the CS on duty for the two tenants and telling them we're investigating. Will update with customer-visible impact.
Eng Oncall - Mira: Short term mitigation: cordon node-ssd-3 and start draining remaining inference pods to other nodes. I can run drain with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-local-data. Any objections?
SRE Jae: go for it. Also scale up Dedicated pool temporarily by 2 nodes in us-west to absorb traffic.
Platform Mike: Initiating autoscaling override (+2 c5gn equivalents) and unpinning a couple modelcache-heavy pods to redistribute.
Eng Oncall - Mira: Running:
```
kubectl cordon node/node-ssd-3
kubectl drain node/node-ssd-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=5m
```
Eng Oncall - Mira: Drain is in progress, but some pods stuck Terminating due to open file descriptors and heavy cache writes.
SRE Jae: If Terminating stuck, force delete may be needed. But first try killing the process inside the pod to flush. Mira, can you exec into one and check logs?
Eng Oncall - Mira: exec'd into inference-runtime-23: tail shows repeated "failed to write checkpoint: ENOSPC" and then a SIGKILL. Kernel shows oom_killer invoked for process 'runtime-server'.
SRE Jae: That explains exit 137. So it's a cascade: disk full -> writes fail -> runtime tries to recover (alloc), hits CUDA OOM because memory fragmentation? Possibly memory + disk interplay due to checkpoint restore.
Platform Mike: I'm purging old rotated logs from /var/log/pods on that node to free immediate space. Command: `sudo find /var/log/pods -type f -mtime +2 -delete` — starting with older than 48h.
Eng Oncall - Mira: Please be careful, preserve current logs for debugging. Recommend move latest logs to S3 rather than deleting. Mike: copy + delete?
Platform Mike: copying top recent artifacts to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1758501234/ then deleting older files. Started rsync now.
Customer Success - Lina: CS update: tenant A experiencing 502s for ~7 minutes now, tenant B intermittent failures. Sending proactive note saying investigation & mitigation underway, ETA 30m.
DevEx Eva: Any chance this is related to recent log verbosity change in runtime v1.9? That shipped last week. If logs grew 10x, that could explain sudden disk fill.
Eng Oncall - Mira: Yes we rolled v1.9 with debug-level modelcache metrics. Rolling back log level on affected nodes might be faster than a full restart.
SRE Jae: Action list so far: cordon+drain node-ssd-3, copy critical logs to S3, purge >48h logs, scale up capacity, redistribute pods. Assign ownership: Mira (exec + drain), Mike (log copy + node cleanup), Jae (incident lead & customer impact), Lina (customer comms).
Eng Oncall - Mira: After freeing ~40GB, drained 80% of pods. A couple of modelcache restore tasks still failing on target nodes due to missing shard files — appears some cache writes were interrupted.
Platform Mike: For the interrupted shards, I'm triggering a rebuild job to repopulate cache from origin storage. That should reduce restore attempts hitting disk.
SRE Jae: We're seeing error rate falling for tenant A — 502s dropping. Still monitoring latency.
Customer Success - Lina: Tenants acknowledged ETA and appreciate the proactive update. No escalation yet.
DevEx Eva: Creating a quick rollback patch to v1.8 (log level restore) for the runtime image. Will push canary to one node group.
Eng Oncall - Mira: Canary deploy applied. New pods come up with less verbose logs. Disk usage trend on us-west nodes shows downward slope.
SRE Jae: Can we confirm root cause hypothesis: increased log volume from v1.9 + slow logrotate + large model cache writes causing ephemeral disk to saturate -> eviction -> process restarts -> CUDA OOM observed during restore attempts?
Platform Mike: That's consistent with node metrics and timestamps. Also found a failing logrotate cron on node-ssd-3 due to permission error — fixed that now.
SRE Jae: Next steps: 1) add guard in orchestrator to prevent large simultaneous cache-write restores when node disk > 75% 2) revert default log level for v1.9 3) add alert for /var/log/pods growth rate 4) postmortem.
Eng Oncall - Mira: I'll leave node cordoned until we've validated rotations + cache rebuild. Ready to handoff to daytime oncall in 30m.
SRE Jae: Handoff: summarize actions + current state in the oncall channel. If error rate rises again, page SRE pagers.
Customer Success - Lina: I'll send a follow-up to affected customers with root-cause note and mitigation timeline once postmortem draft is ready.
Incident Bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated -> monitoring. Root cause candidate: log bloat + failed logrotate + large cache writes -> ephemeral exhaustion -> pod eviction -> runtime restarts -> CUDA OOM during cache restore.
SRE Jae: Thanks all — great rapid coordination. I'll open INC-175850 for the postmortem and assign owners: Mira (drain + runbooks), Mike (logrotate fix + cleanup), Eva (rollback PR + deploy), Lina (customer comms).
Eng Oncall - Mira: handing off to daytime oncall @SRE_Day. Leaving channel open for any follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
